source_read: Accepted manuscript PDF, 45 pages: text pp. 1-8 read in full; reference list (pp. 8-40) skimmed. Tables 1-5 (PDF pp. 41-45) read, and Table 3 (PDF p. 44) parsed with word coordinates to recompute the across-drug medians. Numbers checked on rendered PDF pp. 4-7, 43 and 44.

claims.overstatement: None for the figures attributed to Ketola & Kriikku. Two small points. (1) 'Tenfold or larger differences between drugs for most specimens' understates Table 3: every one of the ten specimens spans more than tenfold between drugs (other blood 16-fold up to bile over 2,000-fold). Many per-drug cells, though, rest on 1-3 results. (2) The claim's later summary calls this 'an unappraised compilation dominated by published poisoning cases'. 'Unappraised' is right. 'Dominated by' is an inference the paper does not state or quantify. The authors say some included studies focus on intoxications and that compiled femoral levels usually exceed the Finnish all-cause reference (Table 2 median 3.35 times). About 87% of results come from the literature (1,442 of 10,993 from the lab). 'Weighted toward poisoning cases' would be closer to the source.
claims.note: Editors' check: the Median row of Table 3 is the median across drugs of the per-drug median ratios. I reproduced every value by parsing the table: other blood 1.27 (41 drugs), vitreous 0.45, muscle 0.985 (printed 0.99), liver 5.06, kidney 2.86, brain 1.84, heart 2.03, lung 3.685 (printed 3.69), spleen 4.25, bile 5.52. The N values in the magnitude (576, 356, 385, 1,697, 401, 565, 185, 187, 71, 537) are the total results per specimen, printed beside the 'Adjusted mean' row; they sum to 4,960, as the text says (about 57% of Table 2's 8,689). Between-drug ranges are confirmed: other blood 0.90 (hydroxyzine, N 6) to 14.61 (chloroquine, N 2); vitreous 0.03 (ephedrine N 1; sertraline N 11) to 1.59 (fentanyl, N 6); liver 0.95 (pregabalin, N 3) to 54.29 (sertraline, N 29). Morphine other blood 1.26 (N 53) and methamphetamine 1.50 (N 9) are confirmed. The paper names no excluded drug: it says drugs used non-medically for which no normal range is available or reasonable were excluded (the paper's category). Cocaine, MDMA and cannabinoids are absent from Table 1's 50 compounds, so 'left out' is accurate. In the Finnish data, autopsy sampling was on average 7 days after death.

anchors.locator: Experimental › Material and Methods, 1st paragraph; Table 1 (PDF p. 41)
anchors.extracted: Finland: post-mortem toxicology in about 6,500 cases a year, requested by the forensic pathologist. Samples are taken at autopsy, on average 7 days after death. The national THL database for 2000-2018 supplied the 50 drugs with the most quantitative results in specimens other than blood, urine or vitreous. Drugs used non-medically for which no normal range is available or reasonable were excluded (the paper's category) (none named; Table 1 lists no cocaine, MDMA or cannabinoid). Combined with literature found by keyword searching and reference lists: 10,993 results from 5,375 cases in 388 studies. Studies with only blood or urine values were excluded.

anchors.locator: Material and Methods, 2nd paragraph; Results and discussion, 1st and 3rd paragraphs
anchors.extracted: Table 3 uses only cases with the femoral blood value. A ratio was computed per case and the median per drug and specimen presented. Table 2 instead divides each median specimen concentration by the Finnish all-cause femoral median (Launiainen & Ojanperä 2014). The laboratory analysed 118,990 cases in 2000-2018 and contributed 1,442 results.

anchors.locator: Table 3, 'Median' and 'Adjusted mean' (N) rows; Results and discussion, 4th paragraph
anchors.extracted: Paired median ratio to femoral blood across drugs (results): other blood 1.27 (576), vitreous 0.45 (356), muscle 0.99 (385), liver 5.06 (1,697), kidney 2.86 (401), brain 1.84 (565), heart 2.03 (185), lung 3.69 (187), spleen 4.25 (71), bile 5.52 (537). Total 4,960 results, about 57% of Table 2. The editors' recomputation from the per-drug cells reproduces each median.

Between-drug spread of the per-drug median ratio: other blood 0.90-14.61; vitreous 0.03-1.59; muscle 0.16-7.24; liver 0.95-54.29; kidney 0.67-34.52; brain 0.10-15.05; heart 0.49-52.15; lung 0.35-55.67; spleen 1.03-31.12; bile 0.51-1,094. Every specimen spans more than tenfold. Other blood: morphine 1.26 (N 53), methamphetamine 1.50 (N 9), amphetamine 1.43 (6), fentanyl 1.15 (33), methadone 1.17 (13), codeine 1.16 (12). Many cells rest on 1-3 results. No range, IQR or interval is given for any ratio.

anchors.locator: Results and discussion, 1st paragraph on the page
anchors.extracted: The ratios varied widely by drug and specimen and with co-medication, intoxication, metabolism, genetics, age, disease and circumstances of death. No correlation was found between the ratio and volume of distribution, half-life or log P in any matrix (data not shown), so these cannot predict a tissue-to-femoral ratio.

Some included studies focus on intoxications and others ignore cause of death; cases could not be classed by cause of death, which was not always given. Post-mortem intervals were not always given and range from hours to months. Femoral levels in Tables 2 and 5 usually exceed the Finnish all-cause reference (Table 2: median femoral ratio across drugs 3.35). Co-medication and similar data are mostly missing. Some drug-specimen pairs have few results and are only suggestive. Sampling site and procedure vary.

key_findings.correction: The paper says cause of death and post-mortem interval were 'not always given' (PDF p. 8), not 'often not given'. Write: 'cases could not be classified by cause of death because it was not always given; time since death was not always given and can range from hours to months'. The rest is confirmed. The same 'often' appears in the card's exposure/outcome text and should change with it.

key_findings.note: PDF p. 7 lists verapamil twice. Table 2 femoral values for propranolol 111.5 and metoprolol 95.0 were checked on rendered PDF p. 43, and chloroquine 24.6 from PDF p. 42.

risk_of_bias.note: AMSTAR 2 by analogy, with all seven critical items unmet, gives critically low confidence. Item 4 'no' is right: keywords and reference lists are given but no database, so not even a partial yes.

interpretation_gap.note: I agree it is 'substantial'. One small correction to 'results_show': every one of the ten specimens spans more than tenfold between drugs, not 'most' (other blood 0.90-14.61, 16-fold; vitreous 53-fold; muscle 45-fold; liver 57-fold; up to bile over 2,000-fold; editors' calculation from Table 3). The extremes often rest on 1-2 results (chloroquine other blood N 2; clozapine muscle N 1).

missed: Table 3 (PDF p. 44) prints a number of results without a value in some cells (ephedrine other blood N 0; oxazepam kidney N 0 and brain N 1). This is a minor internal inconsistency.
For cl_gen_deaths_level_changes: the claim (and the card's interpretation gap) say the between-drug differences are tenfold or larger for 'most' specimens; Table 3 shows this for all ten.
